newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:

* The House approved a bill freeing $215 million to support family-planning programmes overseas, but also approved a separate measure to prevent the money from going to groups that perform or endorse abortions.

* President Clinton retains strong ties to friends, associates and supporters from Arkansas despite the questions some of these relationships have raised, ranging from those in the Whitewater investigation to those in his campaign funding efforts.

* The Dow industrials crossed 7,000 for the first time on Thursday, surging 60.81 points to close at 7,022.44. Despite historical patterns in which the blue chip indicator has fallen sharply or risen only slightly after two years of gains exceeding 20 points, the Dow -- which gained 33 percent in 1995 and 26 percent in 1996 -- shows few signs of slowing.
* Connecticut Governor John Rowland proposed a two-year budget that would cut state income taxes by about $380 million in 1998 and reduce the state's work force by about 10 percent.

* Many of an estimated 110,000 Hong Kong Chinese who have arrived in Vancouver, British Columbia, over the last decade are straddling two worlds until they can return to Hong Kong with the protection of a Canadian passport.

* Three homeless men who burned to death on Wednesday night as they tried to warm themselves around an open fire had created a world for themselves along the boardwalks of Brighton Beach, where they are remembered by friends and social workers.
